test_cases.brief_summary: Weekly newsletter 'Shelf Life' about independent bookstores — business story behind indie retail, targeting book lovers and publishing professionals, smart/warm tone, free with future paid tier — existing example, full 5-step pipeline
test_cases.editorial_naturalness_note: Zero tells. The pilot edition opens with 'A bookstore that small should not work' — a thesis sentence that earns the second sentence without throat-clearing. The welcome email avoids every automated-marketing cliché: 'I am not writing this as a cheerleader for indie bookstores' establishes a real editorial voice. Subject line #2 ('The bookstore that fired its reading chair') demonstrates genuine headline craft.

test_cases.brief_summary: Daily newsletter about remote work culture — 'how distributed teams actually function,' targeting remote workers and HR leaders, data-driven/punchy tone, paid from launch on Beehiiv — simulated deliverable, full pipeline
test_cases.editorial_naturalness_note: Two tells: 'remote work' is a high-saturation topic where LLM defaults ('the future of work,' 'hybrid is here to stay') are harder to avoid. The welcome email for a paid-from-launch product needs billing/value language that the agent's template doesn't natively handle, producing slightly generic 'what you get' framing.

test_cases.brief_summary: Monthly newsletter about European contemporary art photography, targeting collectors and gallery professionals, high-register/curatorial tone, free on Substack — simulated deliverable, full pipeline
test_cases.editorial_naturalness_note: Niche, high-register content plays to the agent's strengths — the positioning document benefits from a narrow, well-defined whitespace. The pilot edition for visual-heavy content is limited by the text-only medium; the landing page copy for a curatorial audience requires restraint the agent handles well.
